chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Basie's band personnel in 1946 and the one record he made before Omaha
summary: Jones lists Jacquet, Buddy Tate, Preston Love and trombonists in the 1946 band, and explains he played just one record before leaving for Omaha.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: No, I'm speaking of '46 when I came out of the Army, who was sitting in the band at the time.
I see. Illinois Jacquet was there now?
He was there and Buddy Tate of course; Preston Love; Jack Washington -
He was a trumpet player, right, Preston?
No, alto. He was a protege of Earl's. There's a very unique story of that which he's written in a book which Johnny Otis wrote. It tells a whole lot of different things.
It's quite a different band now. Who else was on trombone besides J. J. ?
Dickie was there. You know I was in the Army and you know how it was, people were being drafted
and you had people to sit in and what have you. Eli Robinson was there, you know, lately just deceased. You know Eli. He was in and out.
Sure, he was playing and arranging.
Trombone. Then we had picked up Cuffy, you remember the great trombone player Cuffy that used to be with McKinney Cotton Pickers. By the time Cuffy had had his career but it was all right.
This was more or less the band that made "The King" with Illinois Jacquet?
Shadow Wilson was playing with the band, but you made the record, "King"?

I made the record, yes, one record. I only played one record on that particular date and then I went and caught the train and went to Omaha. Earl Warren went back in the band so that Preston could go home and visit his family. That's how you saw me in Omaha.
